title: Liquid-Water Sensible Enthalpy Contract

invariants.evidence: Adds one solver-independent energy primitive to the single SWAP5 kernel/process architecture; no use-case-specific SWAP implementation is introduced.
Production code contains no file, path, parser, format or unit-number dependency.

Liquid-water thermophysical properties are explicit parameters and computed storage/transport energies are result data; no forcing, numerical policy or dynamic state is mixed into the parameter object.
EB-I04 adds no persistent per-column physical state or restart payload.
The algebraic routines require no Newton vectors, Jacobians or other persistent scratch; no worker scratch is moved into column state.
The primitive is scalar and layout-agnostic, but batched/SoA/SIMD execution and cache behavior are not qualified here.
The routines mutate no committed state and are safe to evaluate during a trial, but transaction-aware publication into an accepted energy ledger is explicitly deferred.
All evaluations are deterministic and cheaply recomputable from the same explicit inputs; no hidden history is introduced.
The contract uses generic storage endpoints and oriented transport amounts; no day, month, year, midnight or fixed step duration is fundamental.
No coupling-window size or calendar boundary is encoded.
The primitive is designed for later transactional coupling/conservation composition but does not itself wire coupling or runtime publication.
No groundwater head/flux interface contract is changed. Groundwater-carried sensible energy requires an explicitly supplied transport amount and temperature in a later composition.
EB-I04 neither modifies nor repairs any water balance; energy calculations consume already defined water storage/transport amounts and cannot create or destroy water.
No groundwater response tangent or sensitivity contract is changed or added.
The algebraic evaluation requires no extra full SWAP run or predictor/corrector solve.
No heavy per-column solver instance or persistent state is added, but hundred-thousand-column throughput is not benchmarked in this workunit.
The primitive is per logical SWAP column/control volume and contains no MODFLOW-cell fraction or tile aggregation logic.
No deep-vadose component behavior is changed.
No deep-vadose/direct-coupling transition logic is changed.
The sensible-enthalpy law is independent of a particular Richards implementation and can consume transport from any soil-water solver that satisfies the later common transport contract.

The implementation reuses the admitted SWAP liquid-water property values only as test/reference inputs while keeping production properties explicit; no legacy global state or module boundary is imported.
No HeadCalc or soil-water-solver internal arrays are referenced.
Physical thermophysical parameters are explicit and no numerical policy silently changes them. Missing vapor/ice/phase-change physics is represented as out of scope, not approximated away.
Operations are constant-cost scalar algebra, but bounded-cost behavior at full runtime/MultiSWAP composition scale is not independently measured or qualified here.
Current canonical thermal/reference physics remains byte-identical and available; EB-I04 does not replace the reference solver.
Status codes and decomposition residuals are available locally, but runtime-wide diagnostics, provenance and reporting are deferred to later composition.
The capability allocates no optional persistent state; unused columns incur no state memory cost from EB-I04.
Donor-temperature choice, tile aggregation, groundwater composition and energy-ledger publication remain runtime/coupler responsibilities outside this primitive.
No .swp input, filesystem, midnight, one-day or mandatory-MODFLOW assumption exists in production code.
EB-I04 is explicitly assessed against all 30 SWAP core architecture invariants in this audit.

hard_nonclaims: No full SWAP5 energy balance is qualified.
No complete soil enthalpy or total sensible-storage law is qualified.
No vapor sensible or latent transport is represented.
No ice storage or freeze/thaw latent heat is represented.
No pressure enthalpy, salinity effect or temperature-dependent liquid-water property law is qualified.
No donor/upwind temperature rule for internal or boundary water transport is qualified.
No precipitation, irrigation or groundwater temperature physics is inferred.
The liquid-water theta_avg*DeltaT contribution must not be double-counted against the admitted De Vries sensible-storage term in a later composition.
Gas/air sensible storage under changing water content remains unresolved for full-soil closure.
Runtime commit/rollback publication, large-batch MultiSWAP throughput and bounded-cost behavior are not qualified.
Independent verification and canonical admission are not claimed.
